html:
SMTO-GWT-0040 — The terminal this step needs isn't open

GUID: 68abbf01-f924-4b4a-b225-ff703d6e7739
Slug: terminal-session-required
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • This step needed a specific terminal window (a command line on the computer), but that terminal was closed or had stopped. The step may have been partly sent before the terminal went away.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: read the Task's latest output in the conversation and look at what changed on that computer. The terminal closed during this step, so the command may already have run or partly run.
  2. If this conversation uses the Code workspace, open Editor commands and choose Open terminal to see whether the terminal is still running. SMTO can only send commands or typing to a terminal that is open and running.
  3. Only if the command did not run, ask SMTO in the conversation to continue the Task or run that step again. Running a command twice could repeat a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The terminal is open and the Task continues past this step without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the same command into a new terminal until you know whether the first one ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A terminal execution, input, output-mirroring or detach action had no active terminal session: no session ID was supplied, the Gateway had no active session with that ID, the terminal process had exited, or a background action needed an interactive terminal that was unavailable.

What this means

  • A terminal action lacked a session identifier, looked up no active session, or found that the retained terminal process was no longer alive. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A terminal action lacked a session identifier, looked up no active session, or found that the retained terminal process was no longer alive.

How to diagnose it

  • Match the requested session ID with the selected Gateway's active terminal and inspect whether an earlier command is still running separately.

How to fix it

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened: inspect the run's trace and the target's current state before sending more input. Then open or reconnect the intended terminal session (the workspace terminal for that run) and continue the run; never replay terminal input or a detached command whose delivery is uncertain.
  • Open or reconnect to the intended terminal session through the existing terminal controls, then inspect its current state before sending input.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended live terminal is attached and its state is understood before new input or execution.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
